answer: Weight requires a public museum to hold one artwork of the identity on a registered loan: curators authenticate provenance, insure it and catalogue it under the owner's key, one loan per identity. An onyx-inlaid panel with forged papers fails pigment tests. Each fake costs one genuine artwork: 2,000 units to buy and insure, 250 in loan and copper appraisal fees, plus 60 days to authenticate. One piece cannot back two identities: the museum holds the original and rejects a second loan of the same ivory carving; a proven forgery revokes the cluster and bars the forger from museum loans.
